name: Beamline 8.3.2 — Hard X-ray Micro-Tomography
measurables: microstructural evolution over time during in-situ processing
phase and void distribution in composites and rocks

probe.flux_notes: ALS beamline page lists flux as '~105 hv/sec/um2 with multilayer' (superscript formatting lost in page rendering; superbend source, critical energy 11.5 keV per beamline manual)

resolution.spatial_notes: Manual states 'Measured 2D resolution: 1.5 um'; beamline homepage states 'resolution of approximately 1 micron'. Effective pixel sizes 0.33 um (20x lens, PCO.edge) to 6.5 um (1x lens, PCO.4000); fields of view 0.8 mm to 16.6 mm depending on lens/camera.
resolution.energy_notes: Resolving power listed as 'White beam / 1% / 0.02%': white light mode, W/B4C multilayer monochromator (8-45 keV, 1% bandpass), or Si(111) crystal (6-46 keV, 0.015% bandpass).
resolution.temporal_notes: Per-projection exposure times: >1 sec (Si(111)), 0.1-2 sec (multilayer), 5-100 msec (white light); typical scans 360 to 1800 images over 180 degrees. White-light flux enables micro-CT 'collected at short intervals to track quickly changing features'.

sample_constraints.size_notes: Robot sample-exchange limits: 0.8 inches wide x 1 inch long x 2 inches tall; stage travel ~10 cm x 10 cm; cylindrical samples preferred with roughly constant ~30% x-ray transmission during rotation; avoid vertically-crossing wires/screws and highly absorbing containers. Sample-detector distance variable from ~1.5 cm to 1.5 m to control phase contrast.
special_requirements: sample sits in open air of the hutch (beam exits through Kapton window)

sample_environments: in-situ high-temperature environments that mimic atmospheric entry (demonstrated in ALS science highlight on NASA superlight ablators)
detectors: PCO.edge sCMOS camera (2560x2160 pixels, 16-bit, 30 fps full frame)
PCO.4000 CCD camera (14-bit, 0.75 fps full frame)
scintillators: Crytur LuAG:Ce (20, 50, 500 um thick), YAG:Ce (Hilger, 50x10x1 mm), CdWO4, GGG

data_products.type: raw projection radiograph series with .sct header file (typical dataset 3 to 30 gigabytes)

reconstructed 3d tomogram (normalized, values scaled x32768; reconstructed with Octopus; analysis/visualization with Avizo and FIJI/ImageJ; beamline reconstruction code at github.com/als-computing/microct)

access.mechanism: general user proposal (beamline listed as 'Operational; open to general users'; onsite and remote ALS-operated access modes)

demonstrated_applications: real-time in-situ tracking of multiphase decomposition of NASA superlight ablator heat-shield materials at high temperature
bone microstructure
glass scaffolds
planet formation studies
plant vasculature (including coastal redwood)
rock and volcanic systems
polymer electrolyte fuel cells
austenitic stainless steel

Beamline group homepage: instrument name/description, ~1 micron resolution statement, alias microct@als.

name: COSMIC Imaging (Beamline 7.0.1.2)
measurables: oxidation state and redox state distribution
elemental and chemical speciation via near-edge absorption

probe.flux_notes: Coherent/monochromatic flux at 1 keV: 1E9 photons/second; source is EPU3.8 elliptically polarizing undulator (38 mm period, 10 mm minimum gap); 50 nm spot size

resolution.spatial_notes: Record soft X-ray ptychography: 5 nm spatial resolution in 2D (Shapiro group, Nature Photonics) and world-record 11 nm spatial resolution in 3D ptychographic tomography (2018, Nature Communications, lithium iron phosphate battery nanoparticles). During COSMIC commissioning, 11 nm resolution (Fourier Ring Correlation, half-bit threshold, 200 ms exposures) was demonstrated in 2D ptychography; conventional STXM zone-plate-limited Rayleigh resolution ~55 nm with 45 nm outer-zone-width optic; beamline spot size 50 nm.
resolution.energy_notes: Entrance-slitless collimated plane-grating monochromator (100 or 300 lines/mm) providing energy resolution suitable for near-edge X-ray absorption spectroscopy; E/dE not quoted on sources used.

sample_constraints.size_notes: Samples must be TEM-compatible ('Any TEM compatible' per beamline page); mounted via FEI CompuStage load-lock system derived from an FEI CM200-series TEM, accepting standard commercial TEM sample holders (e.g., 3 mm grids); transmission geometry favors thin, soft-X-ray-transparent specimens.

sample_environments: cryo-capable TEM sample holders (via FEI CompuStage manipulator)
sample rotation for nano-tomography
commercial fluid-flow electrochemistry TEM holders (advanced sample environment under development per 2018 beamline paper)
detectors: fast frame-rate CCD (Berkeley Lab-developed high-speed detector, ~100 frames/s, ~400 MB/s) for ptychographic diffraction data
small-area silicon PIN diode (total transmission detector for conventional STXM; motorized retraction for switching to diffraction/ptychography mode)

data_products.type: 2d STXM images and spectromicroscopy image stacks

access.mechanism: general user proposal (onsite and ALS-operated remote access)

demonstrated_applications: 3d redox-state mapping of lithium iron phosphate battery cathode nanoparticles at 11 nm resolution
3d chemical imaging of nanoparticle clusters harvested from a rechargeable coin-cell battery
ptychographic imaging of nano-structured Fe3O4 battery anode particles (primary particles ~10 nm)
magnetic domain imaging of FeGd multilayer films with circularly polarized X-rays at the Fe L3 edge (~100 nm domains)
nanoscale imaging for battery electrochemistry, fuel cells and catalysis, and cement nanocrystal analysis

provenance.notes: Primary beamline page: energy range 250-2500 eV, EPU3.8 source, technique list, 50 nm spot size, coherent flux 1E9 ph/s at 1 keV, 'Any TEM compatible' sample requirement, access modes, contacts, status.
Record resolution figures: 5 nm 2D ptychography and 11 nm 3D ptychographic tomography; high-speed detector; applications.
Confirms 11 nm 3D record on coin-cell battery nanoparticles; CCD ~100 fps (~400 MB/s); SHARP reconstruction on GPU cluster (CAMERA).

Shapiro et al. 2018 (doi:10.1017/S1431927618012485): probe details, imaging branch design, STXM ~55 nm Rayleigh resolution, 11 nm ptychography by FRC during commissioning, detectors, TEM-holder-compatible stage, FeGd and Fe3O4 demonstrations, planned fluid-flow electrochemistry holders and rotation for nano-tomography.
ALS access by General User Proposal or beamtime request through ALSHub.
COSMIC BL 7.0.1.2 FEI CompuStage load-lock accepting TEM sample holders, cryo-capable; basis for sample_constraints and sample_environments.

name: SIBYLS Beamline (Beamline 12.3.1)

techniques.name: small-angle X-ray scattering
variants: SEC-SAXS (size-exclusion chromatography coupled, with inline UV/MALS/QELS/refractometry)

measurables: conformational ensembles and macromolecular flexibility in solution
oligomeric state and assembly of macromolecules and complexes in solution
molecular weight in solution (via inline SEC-MALS)

probe.flux_notes: ALS beamline directory: 10^11 ph/sec (resolving power 0.001, superbend source). Classen et al. 2013: SAXS flux (uncollimated, 500 mA) 2x10^13 photons per second; MX flux (collimated, 100 um, 500 mA) 2x10^11 photons per second; wavelength range 0.73-2.5 Angstrom via customized Kohzu APM-type monochromator with both Si(111) crystals and Mo/B4C multilayer optics

resolution.energy_notes: ALS directory quotes monochromator resolving power 0.001 (dE/E); dual-mode Si(111) / multilayer monochromator
resolution.spatial_notes: q-range 0.01-0.4 inverse Angstrom is the standard SEC-SAXS/mail-in configuration (wavelength 1.127 Angstrom, sample-to-detector distance 2100 mm); Classen et al. 2013 report accessible q from a minimum of 0.007 to a maximum of 4.2 inverse Angstrom with tunable wavelength allowing q-range adjustment without changing sample-to-detector configuration

sample_constraints.size_notes: HT-SAXS mail-in: 'Three sample concentrations between 1-10 mg/ml'; 'Fill plate wells with a consistent volume of 30uL of sample and buffer' in '96-well Full-skirt Clear (not opaque) PCR Microplates'. SEC-SAXS: 'The sample concentration should be from 3-10 mg/ml with smaller molecules requiring higher concentrations'; 'A sample with a minimum volume of 60 ul'; users supply '50 ml of 10x SEC buffer' per run
special_requirements: HT-SAXS: do not use greater than 2% glycerol
HT-SAXS: collect two identical matched buffers for each concentration series, one before and one after
SEC-SAXS: salt concentration must not exceed 500 mM and buffer pH must be less than 7.5
SEC-SAXS: each beamtime slot is limited to 7 samples using 1 column and 1 buffer

sample_environments: Hamilton ML4000 liquid-handling robot for 96-well plate SAXS
SEC-SAXS with inline UV (280 nm), MALS, QELS, and refractometry detection
SEC columns: Shodex PROTEIN KW-802.5 (150 kDa exclusion limit), KW-803 (700 kDa), KW-804 (1000 kDa)
detectors: Dectris Pilatus3 2M pixel array detector (SAXS endstation, installed August 2015)
ADSC Quantum 315r CCD (MX endstation, per Classen et al. 2013; 2-theta -5 to +45 degrees)

data_products.type: merged SAXS curve per sample with report including SAXS parameters and P(r) function (SEC-SAXS)

typical_experiment_duration: HT-SAXS: 48 samples and 48 alternating buffers (a full 96-well plate) completed in about 4 h; SEC-SAXS: 25 min elution per sample, 7 samples per beamtime slot

access.mechanism: General user access (onsite and remote-robotic); high-throughput mail-in SAXS via MailinSAXS slot reservation — users register a MailinSAXS account, register with the ALS User Office, and submit one ALS RAPIDD proposal for every three MailinSAXS slots
access.cost_model: Funded by DOE BER and NCI; supported by IDAT, SBDR, ALS-ENABLE, and the DOE

demonstrated_applications: lipid nanoparticle structure characterization
protein conformational analysis via SEC-SAXS
polymer chelator structure-function relationships
solution scattering of DNA/protein complexes, flexibility, conformational states, and assembly structures
SAXS- and AlphaFold-guided atomistic modeling (BilboMD, FoXS)

provenance.notes: Facility/status, technique SAXS, energy range 5,000-17,000 eV, superbend source, flux 10^11 ph/sec, resolving power 0.001, access modes onsite and remote-robotic, contacts, funding.
Beamline name, MailinSAXS/HT-SAXS program, SEC-SAXS, demonstrated applications, analysis tools (BilboMD, FoXS, ScAtter, RAW), support, subpage URLs.

HT-SAXS sample constraints verbatim: 1-10 mg/ml three concentrations, 30 uL per well, 96-well clear PCR microplates, max 2% glycerol, paired buffer blanks; data product 'integrated scattering profiles in ASCI format'.

SEC-SAXS constraints verbatim: 3-10 mg/ml, minimum 60 ul, 50 ml of 10x SEC buffer, salt <=500 mM, pH <7.5, 7 samples per slot, Shodex columns; data products: merged SAXS curve with P(r) report plus SEC-MALS report.

Standard SEC-SAXS configuration: wavelength 1.127 Angstrom, sample-to-detector 2,100 mm, q 0.01-0.4 inverse Angstrom, 2 sec exposures during 25 min elution, inline UV/MALS/QELS/refractometry, RAW and Wyatt Astra 8.

Classen et al., J Appl Cryst 46 (2013): dual SAXS/MX endstation design, wavelength 0.73-2.5 Angstrom, Kohzu APM monochromator, SAXS flux 2x10^13 and MX flux 2x10^11 ph/s at 500 mA, q 0.007-4.2 inverse Angstrom, ADSC Quantum 315r, Hamilton ML4000, 96-well plate ~4 h (pre-2015 configuration). MX technique and MX detector fields rest on this 2013 source; current ALS directory lists only SAXS.
SAXS detector: Pilatus3 2M installed on the SAXS endstation 2015, first user data August 19, 2015; supersedes mar165.
Staff roles: Tainer (Spokesperson), Hura, Hammel, Classen, Holton (Beamline Scientists), Burnett (Administrator); emails from als.lbl.gov directory page.

name: MERLIN High-Resolution ARPES Beamline (Beamline 4.0.3)

techniques.name: spin-resolved angle-resolved photoemission spectroscopy
variants: endstation 4.0.3.3, under commissioning as of retrieval date

measurables: energy gaps and in-gap electronic states

resolution.spatial_notes: Refocused beam spot of ~50x20 um at ARPES endstation (demonstrated); 50 um FWHM spot at spin-ARPES endstation 4.0.3.3.
resolution.energy_notes: Beamline page quotes 'resolving power ~ 25,000' with the 1200 lines/mm high-flux grating; MERLIN design target resolving power 5x10^4. Demonstrated overall ARPES energy resolution as low as 7 meV (Scienta R8000, published measurement).

special_requirements: verbatim from beamline page: 'UHV-compatible solids: UHV cleave, in-situ thin film growth, Sputter-anneal, Sample delivery in Vacuum suitcases'

atomically clean surface required; cleaved-surface quality/inhomogeneity directly affects spectra

sample_environments: liquid He flow cryostat on 6-axis sample manipulator, cooled to as low as 6 K (ARPES endstation, demonstrated)
closed-cycle liquid helium cryostat (spin-ARPES endstation 4.0.3.3)

access.mechanism: general user proposal; beamline listed as 'Operational; open to general users' with onsite access mode

demonstrated_applications: temperature-dependent ARPES of the Kondo insulator SmB6: Sm 4f states, hybridization gap and in-gap states (30-140 eV excitation)
photon-energy-dependent kz band mapping and polarization-dependent (LH/LV) Fermi-edge mapping of single crystals

provenance.notes: Primary source: photon energy range 10-150 eV, EPU9 source, 1200 l/mm grating resolving power ~25,000, selectable polarization, endstation list and status, spin-ARPES specs, verbatim sample requirements, contacts, ALSHub access.

Denlinger et al., 'SmB6 Photoemission: Past and Present' (measured at MERLIN): Scienta R8000, energy resolution as low as 7 meV, LHe flow cryostat to 6 K, UHV better than 8x10^-11 Torr, ~50x20 um spot, 30-140 eV with linear/circular polarization, demonstrated applications/data products.

'MERLIN - A meV Resolution Beamline at the ALS' (design paper): expected flux >10^11 ph/s at resolving power 5x10^4 over 16-130 eV; design purpose. Figures via search snippet — design values, lower confidence.

resolution.spatial_notes: Minimum X-ray spot size 5x5 um to 15x15 um at ES-2 (powder XRD); 30x30 um at ES-1 (single-crystal diffractometer)

sample_environments: diamond anvil cells (axial or radial diffraction geometry), capable of reaching Mbar pressures (1 Mbar = 100 GPa)

resistive (external) heating of samples in a diamond anvil cell to >1500 K
ambient-pressure heating to ~1000 C with simultaneous controlled atmosphere
detectors: Dectris PILATUS3 X CdTe 300K (ES-1 single-crystal diffraction; operational from spring 2023 cycle)

demonstrated_applications: stress-induced structural transformations, elastic strain, and defect evolution in gold nanocrystals tracked by in situ XRD under pressure cycling
